AI Summary

Three papers in this window are worth reading in full. Li et al. in Molecular Cell resolve the TE-derived splicing landscape across pan-cancer samples and define TEtrans: transcripts that initiate inside transposable elements, splice within or between TE loci, and are built predominantly of TE sequence rather than host exons. One ERV-derived TEtrans promotes colorectal cancer growth through topoisomerase I-mediated DNA relaxation, and a subset encodes shared tumor antigens that elicit antigen-specific cytotoxic T cell responses, with a murine counterpart mediating antigen-dependent tumor control in vivo. This is the field moving from which TEs are on to what transcript architecture they build, the same question the lab's IFNAR2 Alu-derived decoy receptor answers for a single immune gene, now asked genome-wide and in the CRC setting where LTR10 was defined. Lin et al. supply the enhancer-side counterpart: quantifying enhancer RNA transcription from GTEx across 41 tissues, they find 47% of transcriptionally active enhancers are sex-biased in at least one tissue, and that many are primate-specific and arose by TE exaptation, with the contributing TE families enriched for binding sites of sex-associated transcription factors. That is MER41 and LTR10 logic applied to a new axis. On the preprint side, Goubert et al. release GraffiTE v1.1, which genotypes structural variants, annotates polymorphic mobile elements, and maps allele-specific CpG methylation through pangenome graphs in one pipeline; in 20 Quebec genomes it typed 4,908 Alu, 704 LINE1, 112 SVA and 21 HERVK polymorphic insertions contributing 144,748 CpGs absent from the reference, and showed element age predicts demethylation (-0.069 log-odds per log10 years).

Cancer and innate immunity converge on MEK this fortnight. Tanaka et al. in Immunity show that KRAS-mutant cancers carry abundant mitochondrial DNA and high cGAS-STING expression, that MEK inhibition releases mtDNA into the cytosol, and that MEKi simultaneously induces PRKN-mediated mitophagy which caps that release by restraining mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization; blocking mitophagy sustains mtDNA efflux, amplifies cGAS-STING, and converts apoptosis into immunogenic cell death with dendritic cell activation. Since MEK inhibition is the lever that shuts down LTR10 enhancer activity in CRC, this defines a second, mitochondrial branch of what MEKi does to a tumor's innate immune output, and it argues the two branches should be measured together. Calendo et al. make that tractable at scale with TEDEdb, a uniform reanalysis of over 7,000 RNA-seq samples across 220 cell lines and 700 drug treatments that confirms DNMT and HDAC inhibitors as TE inducers and adds CDK and topoisomerase inhibitors as producers of a viral-mimicry signature; it also warns that TE expression is far more batch-sensitive than gene expression. Castiglioni et al. identify an IFN-I-high, immunotherapy-refractory state in colorectal cancer liver metastases defined by loss of IFNAR1 on effector T cells, receptor-level attenuation of type I interferon output in exactly the tumor type where the lab's LTR10 work sits, and Kumari et al. report an oncogenic role for the m6A writer METTL3 in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, though the retrieved abstract is truncated before the mechanism.

The RNA layer is unusually strong. Nan et al. in Nature Genetics build a single-cell alternative polyadenylation atlas from 2 million cells across 379 aged human brains, showing APA changes are largely distinct from expression changes, and deriving cell-type-resolved 3'UTR QTLs for 4,288 genes that preferentially colocalize with protein QTLs over eQTLs; 168 GWAS loci across 17 brain traits depend on 3'aQTLs and only 17.5% are shared with eQTLs, including SNCA, where 3'UTR choice alters mRNA localization. Intronic TEs are a principal source of cryptic polyadenylation signals, so this is the template for asking the same question of TE-driven intronic polyadenylation and premature termination in innate immune genes. Kwon et al. map m6A in lncRNAs at single-base resolution and find deposition spread along the transcript rather than clustered, attributing the difference to TE-derived sequence shaping motif availability and local structure, with m6A also tied to lncRNA polyadenylation, the lab's m6A-on-TE-transcripts question asked in the noncoding compartment. Aharon and Oshlack add a methodological caution for long-read isoform discovery: comparing nanopore direct RNA, direct cDNA and PCR-cDNA across seven SG-NEx datasets, they find reverse transcription and amplification inflate exitron-containing isoforms and systematically undercount highly m6A-methylated transcripts, which is precisely the class of junction and the class of transcript a TE exonization screen is looking for.

Among methods and comparative work, Wang et al. show that fine-tuning Borzoi on model-generated synthetic MPRA variant effects raises Pearson correlation from 0.28 to 0.54 on CAGI5 promoter variants and from 0.39 to 0.46 on 903 GTEx fine-mapped whole-blood eQTLs without degrading any of the 7,611 pre-trained tracks, a credible route to scoring polymorphic TE insertions where no MPRA data exist; Schreiber supplies tangermeme for the interpretation layer on top of such models. Baril et al. release Earl Grey ParTEA for consistent cross-genome TE annotation from one shared non-redundant library, expanding the Drosophila library from 343 to 1,852 families, the prerequisite for any lineage-specific claim in comparative immunogenomics. Two papers show TE insertions doing regulatory work directly: Glatthard et al. trace a bovine failure-to-thrive and immunodeficiency syndrome to a 10.4 kb ERVK insertion in exon 3 of ALKBH8 that introduces a cryptic transcription termination signal truncating the mRNA, the lab's premature-termination mechanism caught in a ruminant population; and Ludwig et al. show that D. simulans resistance to the P-element, Shellder and Spoink arose mostly through insertions into piRNA clusters that pre-date the invasions. Moene et al. round this out by showing that Sleeping Beauty reintegration follows 3D contact frequency of the launch site rather than destination chromatin, so genome folding, not local chromatin state, writes a transposon's insertion landscape.
